title: Paul Zoll made a stopped heart beat again using electricity, and was one of the pioneers of the pacemaker and the defibrillator

trailer.text: According to the Lasker Foundation, in 1952 he demonstrated for the first time that a stopped human heart can be made to beat again by external electric stimulation.
In the following years he developed an external electric shock, a heart monitor with an alarm, and an implanted pacemaker.

glance.label: What he developed
glance.value: External pacemaker, electric shock, heart monitor, implanted pacemaker

stations.title: A boy from Roxbury, a doctor in wartime

paragraphs.text: Paul Zoll was born in Boston on July 15, 1911, to his parents Hyman and Molly.
In 1932 he received a bachelor's degree summa cum laude, and then went on to medical school at Harvard.
He considered going into pathology, because he was unsure whether he was able to treat patients.
In World War II he served at a U.S. Army hospital in the United Kingdom dedicated to thoracic problems.
There he was cardiologist and Chief of Medicine.
During this service he was impressed by the irritability of the heart during surgical manipulations.
According to Encyclopedia.com, during his service he received the Legion of Merit.
According to Encyclopedia.com, from 1941 to 1945

stations.title: The patient who should not have died

paragraphs.text: From 1947 to 1958 Zoll was Chief of the Cardiac Clinic at Beth Israel Hospital.
In the late 1940s he encountered a 60-year-old woman with Stokes-Adams disease, who had suffered seizures for three weeks.
When she died, Zoll was deeply troubled.
He said that a normal heart, with only a block of conduction, should not die, and that it should be possible to stimulate it.
According to the memorial minute, before Zoll's discovery cardiac standstill was a catastrophic and usually terminal event that rarely responded to treatment.

Before he developed, in 1956, a safe and practical technique of external electric shock to stop ventricular fibrillation of the heart, the only approaches were emergency opening of the chest and manual compression of the heart.
In 1950 Zoll passed a wire through a dog's esophagus and produced abnormal contractions of the ventricles.
Later he was able to elicit the same response with stimuli applied externally to the chest.
In 1952 he had the opportunity to try the treatment in a human: a 65-year-old man with end-stage coronary disease, complete heart block and recurrent cardiac arrest.
The external stimulation worked for 52 hours, and the patient lived another six months.
Zoll found that a single electrical stimulus to the surface of the chest could produce a heartbeat in patients with heart block caused by Stokes-Adams disease.
According to the memorial minute, for the first time it became possible to keep a patient alive during cardiac standstill lasting hours or days.
According to SCA Aware, he was the first in the world to electrically pace or defibrillate an arrested heart from the surface of the chest.
The experiments were published in 1952 in a respected medical journal.
Zoll was grateful for an article in the Catholic newspaper The Pilot, in which the editor told his parishioners not to worry about the strange treatment at Beth Israel Hospital.
In the year after the first success, Zoll worked with engineer Alan Belgard of the Electrodyne Company on an effective pacemaker through the surface of the chest.
In the early 1950s Zoll and his technical collaborators developed a monitoring device.
The device displayed the heart's activity on a screen, sounded a tone with each beat, and set off an alarm when the heart stopped.
According to the Lasker Foundation, Zoll developed the theory and technique of continuous monitoring of heart rhythm, and was the first to apply it in patients.
In 1956 Zoll developed a safe and practicable technique of external electric shock, and it was applied successfully in humans.
In 1960 he reported that external electric shock terminates supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular tachycardia and atrial fibrillation.
According to the Lasker Foundation, his later research showed that external alternating current shock also stops ventricular fibrillation.
Between 1960 and 1964 Zoll and his colleagues developed a method for long-term direct electrical stimulation of the heart by an implanted pacemaker.
According to the memorial minute, cardiac monitors and programs for the management of cardiac arrest and arrhythmias are the foundation of modern coronary care units.
According to the Harvard Crimson's report on the reasons given for the Lasker Award, the coronary care unit found in most modern hospitals is based on his work.
The Lasker Foundation states that pacemakers have saved thousands of people from sudden death, and attributes them to Zoll's invention.
According to TIME, Zoll and another researcher were chosen for the award for techniques and devices that save or prolong more than 150,000 lives a year.
The memorial minute states that Zoll will be remembered for the contribution he and his inventions made to the marked reduction in morbidity and mortality from heart disease.
The sources give different figures, from different years, for how many Americans are living with a pacemaker.
According to SCA Aware, electrical rhythm disorders still take about 1,000 lives a day in the United States.
In 1973 Zoll received the Albert Lasker Award for Clinical Medical Research.
He shared the award with William Kouwenhoven, for the development of defibrillators and pacemakers.
Kouwenhoven was also recognized for external cardiac massage.
According to the Lasker Foundation, Kouwenhoven developed a closed-chest defibrillator independently, at the same time as Zoll's work.
Each of the winners received $10,000 and a gold statuette of the Winged Victory of Samothrace.
According to TIME, jury chairman Michael DeBakey said that until the work of the two researchers there was no way of dealing with a heart emergency.
According to SCA Aware, the Lasker Award is called the American equivalent of the Nobel.
According to Encyclopedia.com, the American Heart Association gave him its award of merit in 1974 and 1992.
Thanks to his methods, Zoll was called the "father of modern cardiac therapy."
His scientific work was published in over 50 original papers.
According to a review in the Texas Heart Institute Journal, Stafford Cohen's book presents Zoll as a leading pioneer in the prevention and treatment of life-threatening arrhythmias.
The memorial minute describes Zoll as a man of stern appearance who demanded much of himself.
According to the memorial minute, his patients and their families held him in high regard.
His son Ross assisted him in the laboratory.
According to the memorial minute, Ross was a physicist and, at the time the memorial minute was written, was an anesthesiologist.
He died on January 5, 1999.
According to Encyclopedia.com, he died in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts.
According to Encyclopedia.com, in 1994
According to Encyclopedia.com, respiratory arrest
According to the Harvard memorial minute, she is a science editor
Some of Zoll's colleagues did not receive well the experiments he published in 1952.
Zoll's original approach to the pacemaker was later superseded by a pacemaker inserted through a vein using a catheter.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, זול נולד בבוסטון ב-15 ביולי 1911 להוריו היימן ומולי.
claims.quote: Zoll was born in Boston on July 15, 1911, to Hyman and Molly Homsky Zoll.

claims.text: לפי ההספד, לפני גילויו של זול עצירת לב הייתה אירוע קטסטרופלי ובדרך כלל סופני, שרק לעיתים נדירות הגיב לטיפול.
claims.quote: Previously, cardiac standstill had been a catastrophic and usually terminal event that rarely responded to therapeutic measures.

claims.text: לפני כן, פתיחת בית החזה ולחיצה ידנית על הלב היו הדרכים היחידות.
claims.quote: Previously, emergency thoracotomy and manual compression of the heart were the only approaches available.

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, זול הוכיח לראשונה ב-1952 שלב אנושי שנעצר אפשר לגרום לו לחזור לפעום באמצעות גירוי חשמלי חיצוני.
claims.quote: Dr. Zoll demonstrated for the first time in 1952 that when a human heart stops, it can be induced, by externally applied electric stimulation, to resume beating.

claims.text: ב-1956 פיתח זול טכניקה בטוחה ומעשית של שוק חשמלי חיצוני שיושמה בהצלחה בבני אדם.
claims.quote: In 1956, Zoll developed a safe and clinically practicable technique which was applied successfully in man.

claims.text: בתחילת שנות ה-50 פותח בידי זול ושותפיו הטכניים מכשיר ניטור שמציג את פעילות הלב על מסך, משמיע צליל לכל פעימה ומשמיע אזעקה בעצירת לב.
claims.quote: a practical monitoring device was developed in the early 50s by Zoll and his technical collaborators to display the electrical activity of the heart on an oscilloscopic screen

claims.text: בין 1960 ל-1964 פיתחו זול ועמיתיו שיטה לגירוי חשמלי ישיר ארוך טווח של הלב באמצעות קוצב מושתל.
claims.quote: Between 1960 and 1964, a method was developed by Zoll and his colleagues for long-term direct electrical stimulation of the heart by an implanted pacemaker.

claims.text: זול זכה בפרס Albert Lasker למחקר רפואי קליני ב-1973.
claims.quote: the Albert Lasker Award for Clinical Medical Research in 1973

claims.text: לפי ציטוט הפרס שהובא ב-Crimson, יחידת הטיפול הכלילי המצויה ברוב בתי החולים המודרניים מבוססת על עבודתו של זול.
claims.quote: The entire coronary care unit found in most modern hospitals is based on Zoll's work, the award citation said.

claims.text: ב-1952 קיבל זול הזדמנות ליישם את הטיפול קלינית בגבר בן 65 עם מחלת לב כלילית סופנית, חסם לב מלא ועצירות לב חוזרות. הגירוי החיצוני הצליח במשך 52 שעות והחולה שרד שישה חודשים.
claims.quote: In a 65-year-old man with end-stage coronary disease, complete heart block, and recurrent cardiac arrest, external stimulation was successful for 52 hours, and the patient survived for six months.

claims.text: זול הודה על מאמר בעיתון הקתולי The Pilot, שבו עורך אמר למאמיניו לא לדאוג מהטיפול המוזר בבית החולים בית ישראל.
claims.quote: A very favorably minded editor told his parishioners not to worry about this outlandish treatment going on at the Beth Israel Hospital

claims.text: זול כיהן כראש מרפאת הלב בבית החולים בית ישראל בין 1947 ל-1958.
claims.quote: From 1947 to 1958, he was Chief of the Cardiac Clinic at Beth Israel Hospital.

claims.text: לפי ההספד של הרווארד, זול קיבל תואר ראשון בהצטיינות יתרה ב-1936 ואז עבר ללימודי רפואה בהרווארד.
claims.quote: Having received the A.B. Degree summa cum laude in 1936, Paul went on to Harvard Medical School

claims.text: זול התלבט אם לעסוק בפתולוגיה משום שלא היה בטוח ביכולתו לטפל בחולים.
claims.quote: He gave serious thought to going into pathology, being unsure about his ability to handle patients.

claims.text: במלחמת העולם השנייה שירת זול בבית חולים צבאי אמריקאי בבריטניה שהוקדש לבעיות בית החזה, שם היה קרדיולוג וראש המחלקה הפנימית.
claims.quote: Zoll served at the 160th U.S. Army Station Hospital in the United Kingdom, dedicated to thoracic problems, where he was cardiologist and Chief of Medicine.

claims.quote: Zoll served in the U.S. Army, joining in 1941 as a first lieutenant and ending his term of service in 1945 as a major.

claims.text: בסוף שנות ה-40 פגש זול אישה בת 60 עם מחלת סטוקס-אדמס, שסבלה מהתקפים במשך שלושה שבועות.

claims.quote: using an esophageal wire, was able to produce ventricular extrasystoles in a dog.

claims.quote: Later he was able to elicit the same response with stimuli applied externally to the chest.

claims.quote: He found that a single electrical stimulus to the surface of the chest could produce a heart beat in patients with heart block owing to Stokes-Adams disease.

claims.quote: Now, for the first time, it became possible to keep such a patient alive during standstill lasting for hours or days.

claims.text: הניסויים הקליניים של זול פורסמו ב-1952 בכתב עת רפואי נחשב, אך חלק מעמיתיו לא קיבלו אותם יפה.
claims.quote: not well received by some of his colleagues, who considered this work

claims.text: קרן לסקר מציינת שזול פיתח את התיאוריה והטכניקה של ניטור רציף של קצב הלב והיה הראשון ליישם אותה קלינית.

claims.text: ב-1960 דיווח זול על יעילות הלם חשמלי חיצוני בהפסקת טכיקרדיה על-חדרית וחדרית ופרפור פרוזדורים.
claims.quote: In 1960, Zoll reported the effectiveness of external electrical countershocks in terminating supraventricular and ventricular tachycardia, as well as atrial fibrillation.

claims.text: לפי קרן לסקר, מחקריו המאוחרים הראו שהלם חשמלי חיצוני בזרם חילופין יעיל גם בהפסקת פרפור חדרים.
claims.quote: externally applied, alternating current counter shocks are similarly effective in stopping ventricular fibrillation

claims.text: מוניטורים לב ותוכניות לטיפול בעצירת לב והפרעות קצב הם הבסיס של יחידות הטיפול הכלילי המודרניות.

claims.quote: developed independently, but at the same time as Dr. Zoll's contribution in this respect.

claims.quote: He was held in high regard by his patients and their families to whom he was devoted
